text: Good morning. Here are your AI stories for today, four of them in total.
Let's begin with the big news.
OpenAI has released Images 2.6, and ChatGPT can now create animated GIFs from a text prompt or an uploaded photo.
Before this update, ChatGPT could not make a GIF in a single step.
You can adjust a GIF's animation speed and edit individual frames.
OpenAI says users now generate over 4 billion images per week, up from 3 billion in September.
Images 2.6 is rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users on web, desktop, and mobile.
Now, a story picked for you.
Moonshot AI has released the weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face.
It is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model, and the company calls it its most capable 3T-class model to date.
It has a 1-million-token context window.
Wait, who exactly released Kimi K3.1 Pro, and how long is its context window? I'd like more stories like this about open-weight models.
Compared with Kimi K3, it swaps full-attention layers for Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention layers, for more efficient long-context work.
Another story picked for you.
Ricursive Intelligence has published a preview of Ripple-65B, a general-purpose model.
The company says it scores 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, which it reports as the top result for U.S. open-weight models.
Ricursive estimates development cost was 32 million dollars, about one-tenth of the previous open-weight leader on agentic coding.

The disruption is one example of geopolitical tensions rippling through the global tech industry.
